Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday — great discussion. Per our demo and the SLO qualification questions, I wanted to summarize what we heard and propose the next steps (MAP = mutual action plan). Please review and flag anything we missed.

High-level recap (what you said):
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 300ms for single-turn text generation at average prompt lengths (~120 tokens).
- Throughput: steady-state 120 reqs/s for the real-time pricing feature; spiky peaks up to 400 reqs/s for end-of-day batch scoring windows.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent users ~80, burst concurrency up to ~350 during heavy periods.
- Streaming: yes, streaming responses required for the live UI; chunked token streaming acceptable, final-token termination must be <200ms after last token generated.
- Prefetch/caching: prefix KV caching expected for repeated query patterns.

SLO checklist attached: fintechco_slo_table.xlsx (I filled in the values we discussed). Also attaching the demo recording and a short note with initial performance observations.

Proposed MAP / Next steps:
1) Validation run: We will run a focused performance run with your sample workload (we need a small corpus + request distribution). Action: FinTechCo to share anonymized sample workload + traffic shape by Mon 7/27.
2) Baseline test: Redwood to run baseline on hosted infra and produce a latency/throughput matrix by model variant + quantization by 7/30. Action: Redwood (Marissa, Stephanie).
3) Streaming verification: Redwood SE to validate streaming latency constraints and confirm chunk sizes. Action: Stephanie to follow up with specifics.
4) Decision criteria: FinTechCo to confirm acceptable p95 latency, tail latency, and cost per 1M tokens target.
5) Procurement & next steps: If baselines meet criteria, proceed to Dedicated quote and procurement (we can start with a 3-month pilot).

Questions for you now:
- Can you share an anonymized sample of 1000 requests with token counts and a request time distribution?
- Is there an internal SLA/penalty requirement we should know about for tail latencies?

Thanks — I’ll loop Stephanie (SE) and Vivek (sales lead) into the next steps.

- The 300ms p95 target is for the user-facing pricing endpoint (single-turn). For the internal batch scoring job, we're more concerned about throughput and cost — p95 can be relaxed to ~1s there.
- Streaming: streaming is mandatory for the UI. We expect clients to see first token within 50-100ms and then steady streaming. The 200ms after final token is ideal but we can tolerate up to 350ms in bad network scenarios.
- Concurrency: 80 typical / 350 burst is correct.

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance SLOs & MAP items (FinTechCo) -- Streaming & concurrency details

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks for the notes. A few engineering clarifications from the SE side based on the SLOs you outlined:

1) Streaming first-token latency: We can generally get first token out within 50-120ms on hosted infra for typical prompts (~120 tokens) if the model variant is optimized for streaming and the network from the client to our regional edge is <40ms RTT. If your users are distributed, we recommend regional routing (we can do us-east + us-west).

2) p95 = 300ms: Achievable on hosted for optimized model variants + KV caching for repeat prefixes, but it depends on the request size distribution and whether the feature uses single-turn or multi-turn (KV cache benefits multi-turn). For consistently tight tails, Dedicated with reserved capacity gives stronger guarantees.

3) Throughput / burst handling: For steady 120 reqs/s with bursts to 400 reqs/s, we recommend a burst pool (Dedicated) or an autoscaling policy with warm instances. We can run a baseline to show cost/latency tradeoffs.

4) Concurrency sizing: Based on your numbers, an initial Dedicated pilot with 4-6 GPU nodes (A100 or equivalent) with batching and streaming optimizations should hit targets; hosted may also work with aggressive caching but your tolerance for tail variance will be higher.

Action items from SE:
- Marissa: we'll need the 1000-request anonymized sample + histogram.
- Alex/Priya: confirm target p95 for pricing endpoint vs batch jobs (Alex to confirm exact numbers).
- Redwood (Stephanie & Logan): run baseline tests and share a matrix (latency/throughput/cost) by 7/30.

Attaching a short note with expected test configs and the assumptions I used: redwood_performance_notes.pdf.

Thanks,
